items.title: 60322_John Bubbles oral history interview
items.q: Then the stage manager after that started raising Sane about leaving the stage before the audience quiets.

ctx.x: So finally I decide for Buck I'll go back since he don't know. So I went back up on the stage -- soon as I got on the stage where you go on the stage, Harry Richman quiets the audience down. He says, "Shh-h-h -- you know there's a little speakeasy up the alley where Buck and Bubbles went." Somebody in the back says, "Well, go get 'em." And they start applauding again. We went on and took a bow and come on off.

Then the stage manager after that started raising Sane about leaving the stage before the audience quiets. Well he forgot -- leaving the stage I was going on and forget the whole doggone thing. But I went on downstairs again and my manager heard what he said, then the manager was in my corner because that tied up the show longer by me not going back on the stage, it tied the show up longer, made us more important, you know. And that was

right up Nazarro's alley. He wanted that. But lo and behold, when I go downstairs and get dressed and go out and I tell the manager after what had happened, I told my manager what happened, Nazarro, what had happened. He said, it fit like a glove. It's all right. I said the guy over at the lights made me mad and I just as soon not go on at all.
